Today's fixes solve the wrong problem

Aliases protect addresses you don't care about. Encryption protects content, not access.

Alias services (SimpleLogin, Relay, Hide My Email)
  • Gives you an exit after a breach
  • Stops spam only by killing the alias
  • Aliases are for throwaway signups, not your bank
  • Protects where protection matters least

A spare identity for throwaway signups. Your real address stays exposed.

Encrypted mail (Proton and similar)
  • Strong privacy for message content
  • End-to-end only if both sides use Proton or PGP
  • Otherwise a normal inbox with a spam filter
  • Anyone who knows your address can still reach you

Locks the room. Doesn't guard the door.

And AI filtering? An arms race the receiver loses: a million AI emails cost nothing to send, everything to filter.

duotail.com · Your email address, finally worth something.3

Our insight: bake purpose into the address

Two flaws keep every inbox open. Fix them and the rules write themselves.

Why filters can't fix it

✉

Email favors the sender

Tuned for 99%+ delivery. A front door you must leave unlocked.

⚠

An address says nothing

An arbitrary string, so mail is judged on name and content. Both are faked.

No AI, no guessing. The address is the rule.

The fix: one identity, a purpose tag per relationship

happy.rhino_<purpose>@duotail.com default-closed
👤
Contacts any address
Trusted senders. Always in, at every address.
↻
Subscriptions _news
Mute or unmute any sender. Come back when you want the deal.
⚡
Cold reaches _hello
One email per stranger. Lock the address when it spoils.

If "Your Bank" writes to your alumni address, you know it leaked.

duotail.com · Closed by default. Open on your terms.4
